entry.label: Information theory
entry.description: A mathematical theory of communication and uncertainty. Shannon information concerns the selection and transmission of possibilities under probability and noise; it does not by itself supply semantic meaning or value.
entry.canonical_definition: The mathematical study of the quantification, coding and reliable transmission of uncertainty-bearing signals, including entropy, channel capacity, redundancy and noise.

profile.title: Information theory
profile.canonical_definition: The mathematical study of the quantification, coding and reliable transmission of uncertainty-bearing signals, including entropy, channel capacity, redundancy and noise.
profile.summary: Information theory supplies a mathematical account of uncertainty, coding and communication through noisy channels. It is powerful precisely because it brackets semantic meaning and studies the structure and limits of transmission.
profile.why_it_matters: Systems and cybernetics use information in several senses. Confusing Shannon information with meaning, truth, knowledge or value produces category errors. The mathematical theory can tell us how much uncertainty is reduced, not whether the message is wise, accurate or humane.
key_distinctions: entropy vs disorder as a loose metaphor
historical_lineage: Nyquist and Hartley as technical precursors
Wiener 1948: cybernetic use of information and control
Ashby: information and variety in regulation
logical_antecedents: a set of possible messages or states
practice_connections: ask what uncertainty is reduced for which decision
measure the channel as well as the message
notice what the classification scheme makes invisible
common_misreadings: a message has the same informational value to every observer
profile.editorial_note: Readable orientation and evidence-backed first pass. Not accepted scholarly consensus until named review is recorded.
